sections.html:
Speed in Waukesha mostly depends on who is buying. Someone paying cash needs no mortgage underwriting and no lender's appraisal, so that deal tends to finish first. An agent listing or a sale by owner adds showings, inspections and a loan. Whichever way you go, three pieces of Wisconsin paperwork follow the house to the finish: a condition report, an electronic transfer return and a recorded deed. Learn them now and you can judge each offer by the money you actually walk away with.

Waukesha is the county seat of Waukesha County, in the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The 2025 population estimate is 70,872, a little under the 71,158 counted in 2020. Water comes up with buyers: the city switched from groundwater to Lake Michigan supply in 2023, and typical bills were projected to climb about 50 percent between 2023 and 2027, so be ready for utility cost questions.

Owner-occupied homes in Waukesha have a median value of $315,500 for 2020 to 2024, and owners live in 58.8 percent of housing units. There are 30,567 households, median gross rent is $1,219 and median household income is $83,837 in 2024 dollars. Those are citywide numbers. Condition, lot size and street can push your house far above or below them, so use the median as a loose yardstick and get written offers before you decide anything.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin requires when you sell in Waukesha
sections.html:
Selling a home with up to four units triggers a duty to give the buyer a completed real estate condition report. Wis. Stat. chapter 709 allows 10 days from the date the contract is accepted. When it fails to show up, the buyer gets two business days after that stretch to cancel and take deposits back.

A personal representative, trustee, conservator or court-supervised fiduciary who never occupied the home does not have to complete the form. The same goes for any transfer the fee statute exempts. Inherited a Waukesha house and never lived in it? Ask the probate attorney or the title company whether that exemption reaches you.

The state also bills the grantor a real estate transfer fee. Section 77.22 puts the rate at 30 cents per $100 of value, the same as $3 per $1,000, and the register takes it at recording. Both the grantor and the grantee sign the electronic return. Section 77.24 divides the proceeds: 20 percent for the county, the remainder for the state.

Bills come from the city clerk and treasurer, who collect from mid-December through July 31. After that date the records pass to the Waukesha County Treasurer. Mailing happens by mid-December. A full payment or first installment is due January 31, with later installments on March 31 and May 31. Look at the city's tax page for the dates printed on your current bill.

The city keeps only part of what you pay. This table shows how the levy is divided:

Taxing bodyRate per $1,000Share of tax dollar
City of Waukesha$7.7953.8%
Waukesha School District$5.1235.41%
Waukesha County$1.308.99%
Waukesha County Technical College$0.251.75%

Together the rates total $14.46 per $1,000. A state credit of $1.04 brings the net rate to $13.42. Payment options include the county's online tax site, any Waukesha State Bank branch, the mail, the two 24-hour drop boxes at City Hall and the library, and the Clerk/Treasurer window at 201 Delafield Street. Your title company can tell you how the current-year bill will be shared between you and the buyer.

Valuing property is the assessor's job. Setting and collecting taxes belongs to others. State law asks for the full value a property would ordinarily bring in a private sale. For current open book and Board of Review dates, phone the assessor.

Think the number is off before you sell? The city takes an online Request for Property Review for the January 1, 2027 assessment date. Property record cards on the assessor's site show lot size, building details and tax history, and they make a useful attachment when you weigh offers.

sections.h2: City rules that can slow a Waukesha sale
sections.html:
Permits and property maintenance matter most. The city wants inspections on new construction, alterations and repairs, on electrical, plumbing and HVAC jobs, and on a change in occupancy. A buyer's inspector may ask about unpermitted work, so assemble your permit history early.

Chapter 17 of the city code covers property maintenance. It makes the owner responsible for keeping the structure and exterior in the condition the chapter describes, and it bars occupancy of unsafe or unsanitary premises. Inspectors answer the phone Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the city site carries forms to report tall grass and other complaints. Closing out open violations before you list takes away one excuse for a lower offer.

  • Building permits and occupancy for one- and two-family homes: 262-524-3530.
  • Electrical permits: 262-524-3533. Plumbing permits: 262-524-3534.
  • Property maintenance inspectors: 262-524-3528, 262-524-3532 and 262-524-3545.

sections.h2: How recording a deed works in Waukesha County
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Waukesha County Register of Deeds. A standard document costs $30, and the office takes a check or money order only. Add any transfer fee from your return receipt to that same payment. For questions, call 262-548-7585 or write to recording@waukeshacounty.gov; the office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Do not expect blank deeds or legal advice at the counter. Most sellers lean on a title company or a real estate attorney to draft the deed and file the electronic return. E-recording returns the document right away. Paper filings come back in two to three weeks if you enclose a stamped return envelope.

Weigh net proceeds, timing and effort for each route, because the best fit changes with the house and the calendar.

  • Agent listing. Works for a house in good shape when waiting for showings and a buyer's loan is acceptable.
  • Selling it yourself. Saves the listing fee, but the condition report, showings and contract land on your desk.
  • Cash offer. Matches inherited houses, tenant-occupied homes, properties needing repairs and sellers on a deadline. Insist on the number in writing, and settle who pays title work and recording.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html: Once an offer is accepted, the report clock begins, so finish that form first. Next, line up your permit history, the latest tax bill and your mortgage payoff details. The title company runs the search, and you confirm how taxes will be split. At the table you sign the deed, the return is filed online and the Register of Deeds records the deed. If the house is a cash sale, those same steps happen with no appraisal or underwriting to hold up the date.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Waukesha?
faqs.a: It turns on the buyer. A purchaser with no lender skips loan approval and the appraisal, while a financed listing adds showings, inspections and underwriting. Either way, the condition report is due 10 days after the contract is accepted.

faqs.q: Do I have to fill out a condition report in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: Usually. Chapter 709 of the Wisconsin statutes covers owners of one-to-four unit residential property. Personal representatives, trustees and similar fiduciaries who never lived in the house are excused, as are transfers the fee statute exempts.

faqs.q: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Waukesha sale?
faqs.a: Expect 30 cents per $100 of value, or $3 per $1,000, paid by the grantor at recording. A few transfers, such as those by will or from parent to child for nominal consideration, are exempt under s. 77.25.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property taxes to in Waukesha?
faqs.a: Pay the City of Waukesha Clerk/Treasurer from mid-December until July 31. After that the Waukesha County Treasurer takes over delinquent real estate taxes. The city accepts online payments, mail, Waukesha State Bank, drop boxes and the City Hall window.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after I sell in Waukesha?
faqs.a: Take it to the Waukesha County Register of Deeds. The deed costs $30 to record by check or money order, plus any transfer fee, and the transfer return receipt has to come with it. A title company usually does this for you.
